mainTopic: Benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה, and whether a food's prohibition counts as intent (איסורו חישובו)
overview: On the previous amud, רבא set out to prove that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after its neck is broken. His source is a ברייתא where רבי שמעון says forbidden-for-benefit items cannot become טמא as food, with בשר בחלב as the one exception. The גמרא first asks why רבי שמעון explains that exception with שעת הכושר, since he holds בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה. The answer is that he gives one reason and adds another. רבא then finishes his proof: if the פטר חמור were permitted, it should have been listed too. The גמרא pushes back that the ברייתא may be talking about a case where nobody intended to eat the donkey. That raises the question of why the רבנן treat it as food, and the suggested answer is איסורו חישובו: its prohibition counts as intent. Several משניות are brought to test this idea, and one clearly shows the רבנן require intent for forbidden meat. So רבא concludes that no one holds איסורו חישובו, and he begins a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why give the 'time of fitness' reason for meat and milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון explains that בשר בחלב can become טמא by saying it once had a שעת הכושר. He could simply say it is food that may be given to others, because in his view it is מותר בהנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does רבי שמעון specifically say that meat and milk can become טמא because it once had a time when it was fit to eat? He should get the same result from the simple fact that it is food you are allowed to give to others to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason רבי שמעון gives for treating בשר בחלב as food that can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule is that food which is אסור בהנאה cannot become טמא as food. If בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה, it never falls under that rule in the first place, so it should not need the special reason of שעת הכושר. The question is why he chose a weaker, roundabout reason when an obvious one was available.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is really the case
Why specifically this? Why mention this particular reason?
A time of fitness; a period when the item was fit to eat
Let me derive it instead from; I could get it from

phrases.english: If so,
why specifically does he say about meat in milk
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא רבא quoted, where רבי שמעון admits that meat in milk can become טמא.

phrases.english: that it is because it had a time of fitness?
phrases.notes: Before the meat and milk were cooked together, each one was fine to eat.

phrases.english: Let me derive it instead

phrases.aramaic: דְּאוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא!
phrases.english: from the fact that it is food you are able to feed to others!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier claim, made on the previous amud, that רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'שהיתה לה שעת הכושר' given in רבי שמעון's ברייתא about בשר בחלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה, it is plainly food that may be given to others. It never enters the איסורי הנאה category, so a special reason should be unnecessary.

steps.title: Source that רבי שמעון permits benefit from meat and milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. He learns this from a גזירה שוה on the word 'holy,' comparing it to טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון that meat cooked in milk is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. The פסוק says 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God' when it forbids cooking meat in milk. Elsewhere the פסוק says 'And you shall be holy people to Me' when it forbids טרפה. Just as טרפה is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, so too meat in milk is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the starting point of its question: רבי שמעון really does hold that בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the idea of being 'holy' next to a food prohibition. For טרפה, the Torah itself allows benefit, since it says to throw it to the dogs. So by comparing the two, בשר בחלב gets the same status: only eating is forbidden. This makes the question in Step 1 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to eat
Permitted for benefit, such as selling it or feeding it to animals
Elsewhere; in another place in the Torah
Just as there, so too here; the formula for comparing two cases
An animal with a fatal injury, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Meat in milk is forbidden to eat
and permitted for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God,'
phrases.notes: This is in דברים, in the same פסוק that says not to cook a kid in its mother's milk.

phrases.english: and elsewhere it says:
'And you shall be holy people to Me,'
phrases.notes: This is in שמות, in the פסוק that forbids eating טרפה and says to throw it to the dogs.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה,
phrases.english: just as there it is forbidden to eat and permitted for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה!
phrases.english: so too here it is forbidden to eat and permitted for benefit!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the assumption behind the question in Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון, using a גזירה שוה from the word 'holy' to compare it with טרפה.

steps.title: He gives one reason and then adds a second
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא gives two reasons. First, בשר בחלב is food that may be given to others. Second, even for the Jewish owner himself, it once had a שעת הכושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and then adding another. The first reason is that it is food you can give to others to eat. The second reason is that even for him, the owner, it once had a time when it was fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 1. רבי שמעון did not leave out the simple reason; he was adding an extra reason on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'food for others' reason is assumed, and שעת הכושר is a second, additional point. The second reason shows that it counts as food even from the owner's own point of view, since before cooking he could have eaten it. So the ברייתא's wording is not a sign that רבי שמעון forbids benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: He states one reason and adds another
For him himself; here, the Jewish owner
Also; even

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא — דְּאוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא,
phrases.english: One: it is food that you can feed to others,
and another: even for him himself,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the Jewish owner, who may not eat the meat and milk now.

phrases.english: it had a time of fitness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question from Step 1, which Step 2 had strengthened.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: the stated reason is an additional reason, not the only one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning שעת הכושר suggested that it was רבי שמעון's only reason, as if the 'food for others' reason did not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both reasons apply. שעת הכושר is an extra point showing it counts as food even for the owner.

steps.title: רבא completes his proof about the donkey firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבא's proof concludes. If רבי שמעון allowed benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה, the ברייתא should have listed it next to בשר בחלב as an exception that can become טמא as food. Since it is not listed, he must forbid benefit from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were true that רבי שמעון permits benefit from the firstborn donkey after its neck is broken, the ברייתא should have taught: 'And רבי שמעון agrees about a firstborn donkey and meat in milk, that they can become טמא as food!'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the side question about בשר בחלב is settled, the גמרא returns to רבא's main proof about the פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule is that only food permitted for benefit (or with a special reason, like בשר בחלב) can become טמא as food. If a פטר חמור after עריפה were permitted for benefit, it too would be an exception worth listing. Its absence from the list shows that רבי שמעון holds it is אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so
Breaking the neck, done to a פטר חמור that is not redeemed
The firstborn male donkey
Let it teach; the ברייתא should have said
Agrees; admits an exception
The טומאה that applies to food

steps.whatToRemember: רבא tries to prove that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה, because the ברייתא lists only בשר בחלב as an exception that can become טמא as food. The 'two reasons' answer explains why the wording about בשר בחלב does not weaken this argument. The next step pushes back on the proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two prohibitions. בשר בחלב is only forbidden to eat according to רבי שמעון. The question here is whether the פטר חמור after עריפה is also forbidden for benefit. רבא tries to prove that it is, but the next step pushes back.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, a פטר חמור after עריפה would be אסור בהנאה even according to רבי שמעון, and so it could not become טמא as food. Step 5 shows that the ברייתא's silence can be explained another way.

phrases.english: And if it were so
that after neck-breaking Rabbi Shimon permits it,
phrases.notes: He means benefit from the firstborn donkey, not eating it.

phrases.english: let it teach: 'And Rabbi Shimon agrees
about a firstborn donkey and meat in milk
that they become impure with the impurity of food!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא דִּלְאַחַר עֲרִיפָה שָׁרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about בשר בחלב is resolved, the גמרא returns to רבא's main proof about the פטר חמור.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a פטר חמור after עריפה is אסור בהנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון, which lists only בשר בחלב as an exception that becomes טמא as food and leaves out פטר חמור.

steps.title: The ברייתא Speaks of a Case Without Intent to Eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. If the owner had intended the פטר חמור to be eaten, it really would become טמא as food according to רבי שמעון. The ברייתא left it out only because it is talking about a case where he never had that intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended it for eating, that is true, and it could become טמא as food. But here we are dealing with a case where he did not intend it for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It says the ברייתא's silence about פטר חמור does not show that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reasoned that if benefit were allowed, the ברייתא would have listed פטר חמור next to בשר בחלב. The answer is that donkey meat is not normal food. Without a specific intent to eat it, it never counts as food, so there was no reason to list it, whatever the rule about benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it, meaning he had in mind that it would be eaten
Here, what case are we dealing with? This phrase limits a source to a specific case
A firstborn donkey
Breaking the neck, done to a פטר חמור that was not redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove that רבי שמעון permits benefit. It only shows that רבא's proof does not force the opposite conclusion.

phrases.english: If he intended it [for eating],
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who broke the donkey's neck.

phrases.english: so it is indeed [susceptible to food impurity];
here, what are we dealing with?
Where he did not intend it [for eating].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from Step 4 by limiting the ברייתא to a case without intent to eat.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's silence can be explained by the lack of intent to eat, not by a ban on benefit.

steps.title: Why Do the Rabbis Treat It as Food?
steps.stepSummary: If there was no intent to eat the donkey meat, why do the רבנן still say it can become טמא as food?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason that the רבנן consider it able to become טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the רבנן, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that without intent, the meat does not count as food. But the רבנן hold that it can become טמא as food. So the גמרא needs to know what makes it count as food for them when there was no intent.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who disagree with רבי שמעון here
They consider it able to become טמא
The impurity that applies to food

phrases.english: And what is the reason
that the Rabbis consider it susceptible to impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 5's point that without intent the meat is not food, and asks how the רבנן can still treat it as food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן treat פטר חמור meat as food for טומאה without any intent to eat it.

steps.title: Its Prohibition Counts as Its Intent
steps.stepSummary: The Sages said before רב ששת that the very fact that the meat is forbidden gives it the importance of food. Its איסור works in place of intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said it before רב ששת: because its prohibition is its intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the רבנן's principle: איסורו חישובו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, unusual food needs a person's intent before it counts as food. Here the Torah's prohibition does that job. Because the Torah bothered to forbid eating it, it is treated as something important enough to count as food.

keyTerms.meaning: Since its prohibition is its intent: being forbidden makes it count as food

steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion here is איסורו חישובו: a food's prohibition stands in for intent to eat it. The next steps test this idea, and in Step 14 רבא drops it.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Sheshet:
phrases.notes: These "רבנן" are the scholars of the study hall, not the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Since its prohibition is its intent.
phrases.notes: Being forbidden to eat is what makes it count as food, even without anyone planning to eat it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן hold איסורו חישובו: the prohibition itself gives the meat food status.

steps.title: Challenge from the Carcass of a Kosher Bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this principle using a משנה. A נבלת עוף טהור needs intent before it can become טמא as food. If its prohibition counted as intent, no intent would be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do the רבנן really say that its prohibition is its intent? But we learned: thirteen things were said about נבלת עוף טהור, and this is one of them: it needs intent, but it does not need הכשר. If its prohibition is its intent, why do I need intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the principle from Step 7 by quoting a משנה that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה is forbidden to eat, so by איסורו חישובו it should count as food automatically. Yet the משנה says it needs intent. That suggests the רבנן do not hold of איסורו חישובו at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? This introduces a contradicting source
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
Intent that the item be eaten
Contact with liquid that makes food able to become טמא

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, do they say
"since its prohibition is its intent"?
But didn't we learn:
Thirteen matters they stated
regarding the carcass of a kosher bird,
and this is one of them:
it requires intent,
but it does not require being rendered susceptible.
And if its prohibition is its intent,
why do I need intent?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּנַן מִי אָמַר הוֹאִיל וְאִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle given in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן hold איסורו חישובו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forbidden נבלת עוף טהור still needs intent. If prohibition counted as intent, the משנה's requirement of intent would be pointless.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה about נבלת עוף טהור follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold איסורו חישובו. The רבנן can still hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by assigning the משנה to רבי שמעון rather than to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement of intent fits רבי שמעון, who does not let a prohibition stand in for intent. So the משנה is no contradiction to the רבנן, and their principle of איסורו חישובו stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? It attributes a source to a specific תנא

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא defends איסורו חישובו for the רבנן by assigning the משנה about נבלת עוף טהור to רבי שמעון. Steps 12-13 bring a challenge that this move cannot answer.

phrases.english: Whose is this?
It is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requiring intent for נבלת עוף טהור reflects the רבנן's view, which would contradict איסורו חישובו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who rejects איסורו חישובו. The רבנן keep the principle.

steps.title: A challenge from the first clause of a משנה about forbidden meat
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the carcass of a non-kosher animal needs intent before it can become טמא as food. If its איסור already counted as intent, why would intent be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The carcass of a non-kosher animal, wherever it is found, and the carcass of a kosher bird or חלב found in the villages, need intent to be eaten, but do not need הכשר. And if you say its prohibition counts as its intent, why do I need intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to attack the idea that an item's איסור gives it the importance of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists items that are all forbidden to a Jew, yet it still says they need a person's intent before they count as food for טומאה. If איסורו חישובו were true, the איסור alone would do the job, and no intent would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a non-kosher animal, such as a horse or a donkey
Intent: a plan to use something as food
Making food able to become טמא by having it touch liquid
Villages, where people do not normally eat these things

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The carcass of a non-kosher animal, in any place,
and the carcass of a kosher bird, and חלב, in the villages —
need intent,
but do not need הכשר.
And if you say its prohibition counts as its intent,
phrases.notes: This is the idea from step 7, the one the Sages said before רב ששת.

phrases.english: why do I need intent?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new משנה to test איסורו חישובו again.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן hold איסורו חישובו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires intent for items that are forbidden. That only makes sense if the איסור does not replace intent.

steps.title: The first clause follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this משנה follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold איסורו חישובו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying this משנה is רבי שמעון's view, not the רבנן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same move as step 9. רבי שמעון does not accept איסורו חישובו, so a משנה requiring intent fits his view. The רבנן can still hold the principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? Used to say which תנא a source follows

phrases.english: Whose is this?
It is רבי שמעון.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that no one holds איסורו חישובו.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only shows that רבי שמעון does not hold it. The רבנן may still hold it.

steps.title: A challenge from the next clause of the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The next clause says kosher carcasses need no intent. That implies a non-kosher carcass does need intent, even though it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The carcass of a kosher animal, wherever it is found, and the carcass of a kosher bird, and חלב in the marketplaces, need neither intent nor הכשר. This implies that a non-kosher animal does need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the continuation of the same משנה and draws an inference from it, to challenge איסורו חישובו again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kosher carcasses are eaten by many people, so they count as food on their own. By saying that only these skip intent, the משנה implies that a non-kosher carcass still needs intent. If its איסור counted as intent, it should not need any.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a kosher animal that was not slaughtered properly
Marketplaces, meaning big towns where people do eat these things
This implies: introduces an inference from the wording

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The carcass of a kosher animal, in any place,
and the carcass of a kosher bird,
and חלב in the marketplaces —
need neither intent nor הכשר.
This implies that a non-kosher one needs intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge from the next part of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן hold איסורו חישובו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By implication, a non-kosher carcass needs intent. If איסור counted as intent, it would not.

steps.title: This clause cannot be assigned to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The easy answer, that this clause also follows רבי שמעון, does not work. The end of the same משנה quotes רבי שמעון by name with a different view, so the beginning must be the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say this is also רבי שמעון: since the end of the משנה is רבי שמעון, the beginning is not רבי שמעון. The end teaches: רבי שמעון says even the camel, the hare, the rock badger and the pig need neither intent nor הכשר. And רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because they have signs of a kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the answer from step 11 before anyone can use it here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the end of a משנה names רבי שמעון as disagreeing, the unnamed first part is the רבנן. So the רבנן are the ones who say a non-kosher carcass needs intent. That shows the רבנן themselves do not treat its איסור as intent, and the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces an answer the גמרא is about to reject
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Signs of a kosher animal: split hooves or chewing the cud

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון is the stricter one here. In this case he is more lenient: animals with one kosher sign need no intent at all. The unnamed רבנן are the ones requiring intent.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
whose is this? It is רבי שמעון —
but since the end is רבי שמעון,
the beginning is not רבי שמעון.
As the end teaches:
רבי שמעון says:
even the camel and the hare
and the rock badger and the pig

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לֹא מַחְשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.english: need neither intent nor הכשר.
And רבי שמעון said: What is the reason?
Because they have signs of a kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer from step 11 cannot rescue the principle from the challenge in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible answer that the second clause follows רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא names רבי שמעון separately, so the רישא must be the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא gives up the principle completely
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that everyone, including the רבנן, agrees an item's איסור does not count as intent. He starts to explain the פטר חמור case another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Everyone agrees that we do not say its prohibition counts as its intent. And if its neck was broken, so too...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea of איסורו חישובו. רבא begins a new explanation of the פטר חמור case, and his sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in steps 12-13 could not be answered, so the principle from step 7 is abandoned for everyone. רבא says that where the donkey's neck was broken, the רבנן indeed agree that it cannot become טמא as food, because no one intended it as food. The rest of his explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier approach and starts a new one
Everyone agrees
Its prohibition counts as its intent
Breaking the neck, what is done to a פטר חמור that is not redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: No one holds איסורו חישובו. Being forbidden does not, on its own, make something count as food for טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The earlier explanation of the רבנן is gone, so the סוגיא now needs a new reason for their view on the פטר חמור.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
According to everyone,
we do not say its prohibition counts as its intent,
and if its neck was broken —
phrases.notes: He's back to the פטר חמור. If the owner broke its neck, he clearly never meant to eat it.

phrases.english: so too,
phrases.notes: The sentence doesn't finish here. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא אָמְרִינַן אִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The challenge in steps 12-13 stood, so רבא gives up the principle and starts a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving up the challenged principle and starting a new explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן hold that an item's איסור replaces intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: No one holds that. In the case where its neck was broken, even the רבנן agree that the פטר חמור cannot become טמא as food. Their ruling must refer to a different case, which is explained on the next amud.
